Action taken: revise_motivation

New motivation:
Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) and Group-level BMI are inversely related because, for a given level of energy intake, higher TDEE (due to increased physical activity or metabolism) results in greater calorie expenditure, leading to reductions in body mass and thus lower BMI over time. Conversely, lower TDEE, if not balanced by lower energy intake, tends to cause BMI to increase. However, the effect of TDEE on BMI is dependent on energy intake, which is a critical component of energy balance and body mass regulation.
